still_unresolved: Whether prioritizing closed storage receptacles over open surfaces yields faster target acquisition for objects typically stored inside enclosed containers.
Whether the general listed-order search strategy should be refined to incorporate object-type heuristics for initial receptacle selection.

updates.evidence_basis: Probe navigated to and opened cabinet_1 first per hypothesis guidance, found no soapbar, then successfully acquired soapbar_1 from countertop_1. Target was on an open surface, not in a closed receptacle, costing 2 additional actions (go to + open) before finding it.
updates.guidance: When searching for a target object not visible at room center, recognize that some object types (e.g., soapbar) may frequently appear on open surfaces like countertops even when closed storage receptacles are available. Blindly prioritizing closed receptacles first can incur unnecessary navigation and opening costs if the target is actually on an open surface. Consider inspecting open surfaces early in the search order, or use object-type priors to decide whether to check closed or open receptacles first.
updates.scope: ALFWorld pick-clean-then-place tasks where the target object type is known but not visible at room center, and both closed storage receptacles and open surfaces are available in the admissible action list.

evidence_status.comparative_support: No alternative search strategy (e.g., heuristic prioritization by object-receptacle affinity) has been tested; memory only records this single approach.
evidence_status.feasibility_support: Target soapbar acquired at step 4 after probing cabinet_1 then countertop_1, confirming feasibility of listed-order search.
evidence_status.policy_relevance: Search efficiency directly affects action count before downstream clean/place phases; a more targeted strategy could reduce wasted probes.

functional_contract.available_state: Agent at room center with full list of visible receptacles from entry observation; target not yet visible; inventory empty.
constraints: Must follow the exact listing order from the initial room observation
Must open closed receptacles before inspecting contents
Must pick up the target immediately upon first exposure
Must not perform actions outside the probe sequence until target is acquired
functional_contract.local_function: Navigate to and inspect receptacles sequentially in the order listed in the room observation until the target object is found and picked up.
functional_contract.required_downstream_state: Agent holds the target object (soapbar) in inventory and knows its current location for subsequent navigation to cleaning/destination receptacles.

parsed.incumbent_segment: Sequential receptacle probing following the room observation listing order until target acquisition
parsed.warrant: The incumbent establishes that listed-order sequential probing achieves target acquisition, but no comparative evidence exists to confirm it is the most efficient or preferred search policy. Resolving whether a semantically informed search order outperforms blind listing-order traversal could materially reduce probe steps in future tasks.

parsed.guidance: Navigate to the first receptacle exactly as it appears in the initial room observation text. If it is a closed storage receptacle, open it and inspect for the target object. If it is an open surface, inspect directly. Take the target if found; otherwise halt the local probe after this single inspection.
parsed.hypothesis: Strictly following the textual listing order from the initial room observation, rather than prioritizing receptacles by type (open vs. closed), provides a reliable baseline search strategy that avoids heuristic mispredictions about object placement.

probe_spec.adaptive_policy: Identify the first receptacle named in the entry observation text. Issue a navigation action to that receptacle. Upon arrival, if the observation indicates it is closed, issue an open action. Inspect the resulting observation for the target object type. If present, issue a take action. If absent or if any action fails, halt the probe immediately without proceeding to subsequent receptacles.
probe_spec.evidence_goal: Whether the target object is found at the first textually listed receptacle, establishing if strict listing-order search succeeds on the first attempt compared to type-prioritized heuristics tested previously.
probe_spec.local_function: Navigate to and inspect the first receptacle in the exact textual listing order from the room observation.
probe_spec.realization_pattern: Select the first receptacle mentioned in the initial room description regardless of its type, navigate to it, open it if it is a closed storage receptacle, inspect for the target object, and take it if present; otherwise halt the local probe.
probe_spec.required_downstream_state: Agent holds the target object in inventory if found, or remains at room center with empty inventory if not found, preserving the ability to continue searching other receptacles.
stop_conditions: Target object is successfully taken into inventory.
Navigation to the first listed receptacle fails.
The first listed receptacle is inspected and does not contain the target object.
An open action fails on a closed storage receptacle.

parsed.reason: Previous explorations tested type-based prioritization (open surfaces first or closed storage first). This probe tests the incumbent's strict textual-listing-order constraint by inspecting only the very first mentioned receptacle, providing a discriminative baseline comparison against those earlier type-heuristic experiments.
parsed.scope: ALFWorld pick-clean-then-place tasks where the target object is not immediately visible at room center and both open surface and closed storage receptacles are listed in the entry observation.

public_capability_evidence: Entry observation lists cabinet_4 first among visible receptacles.
Historical capability vocabulary includes 'go to', 'open', and 'take' action schemas.

parsed.rationale: C candidate proposes strict listing-order search to avoid type-prioritization overhead, directly refining the active listed-order comparison. Scope extends from pick-and-place to pick-clean-then-place tasks.
